name: Fixup-style residual scaling
tagline: Kaiming init + Fixup-inspired residual-branch scaling: scale the last conv of every residual block by L^(-1/2) and zero-init its trailing BatchNorm gamma.
pseudocode:
1. For every Conv2d: $\mathrm{KaimingNormal}_{\text{fan\_out, ReLU}}$.
2. For every BatchNorm2d: $\gamma = 1, \beta = 0$.
3. For every Linear: $\mathrm{KaimingNormal}_{\text{fan\_in, ReLU}}$, bias $= 0$.
4. If model is a ResNet: $L \leftarrow$ number of BasicBlocks; $s = L^{-1/2}$.
5. For each BasicBlock: $\text{conv2.weight} \mathrel{*}= s$; $\text{bn2.}\gamma \leftarrow 0$.
6. (For VGG-style nets: stop at step 3; no residual scaling.)

key_hyperparams.name: fixup_scale
key_hyperparams.role: rescale last conv per residual block

key_hyperparams.name: bn2 gamma
key_hyperparams.role: zero-gamma so residual branch starts at identity

diff_from_baseline: Inspired by Zhang et al. Fixup (ICLR 2019) and Goyal et al. zero-gamma trick (2017). Unlike full Fixup, BatchNorm is kept; only the last conv of each residual block is scaled by 1/sqrt(L) and its BN gamma zeroed. Falls back to plain Kaiming init for non-residual nets.

name: Kaiming Normal
tagline: He/Kaiming normal initialization: Conv weights drawn from N(0, 2/fan_out), BatchNorm at (1,0), Linear from N(0, 2/fan_in).
diff_from_baseline: He et al., "Delving Deep into Rectifiers" (ICCV 2015). The de-facto standard for ReLU CNNs; preserves forward-pass activation variance under ReLU. Default initializer in modern image-classification codebases.

name: Orthogonal init
tagline: Orthogonal initialization for Conv and Linear weights with ReLU gain (sqrt(2)); preserves gradient norms and encourages dynamical isometry.
formula: $$W = g\,Q,\quad Q^\top Q = I,\quad g = \sqrt{2}\;(\text{ReLU gain});\quad \gamma_{\text{BN}}=1,\;\beta_{\text{BN}}=0,\;\text{bias}=0$$

key_hyperparams.name: applies_to
key_hyperparams.role: weight matrices reshaped to (out, fan_in*kk) before QR

diff_from_baseline: Saxe et al., "Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear networks" (ICLR 2014). Initializes weight matrices as semi-orthogonal so singular values are 1, preserving gradient norms during backprop and enabling dynamical isometry in deep networks.
